Complete named street circuit follows the northern hairpin and southern return through the city. The independent relation measures 4753.7 m; source coordinates remain unchanged despite the catalogue distance discrepancy.

Northern short course uses the independently named GP Circuit branch and B Course connector, excluding the Permanent Circuit southern loop and overlapping duplicate course way. The catalogue diagram identifies the same northern perimeter and infield return. The operator distinguishes the 3.29 km B Course from the 3.04 km A Course.

Full GP course follows the entire closed portion of the independently named YEONGAM F1 Track way, retaining both the northern GP sector and southern permanent sector. The source way includes a short overlapping prefix outside its closed portion; the recipe uses the actual repeated source node as its closure. The operator identifies the same full configuration at 5.615 km; this independent source measures 5,594.4 m against the catalogue 5,666 m. No coordinates are adjusted.

Open single-lap sprint follows Startline Straight, Woodside, the eastern loop and Shenstone Straight to the finish. The operator course plan identifies the 831 m single-lap route; the independent source-node selection measures 827.9 m. The catalogue scalar 983 m and diagram include untimed approach/run-on areas. Those areas and the alternate Flagpole connector are excluded from the timed draft; both endpoint nodes agree with private start and finish gates.

Open long hillclimb retains the central hairpin and full climbing branch, excluding the shorter bypass and return spur. The operator describes a 1,127-yard course (about 1,030.6 m), consistent with the independent 1,033.1 m timed source path. The catalogue scalar 1,222 m differs; geometry is neither extended nor scaled. Separate endpoint nodes agree with private timing gates.

Open climb follows the forward timed section of the independently named Loton Park Speed Hill Climb source way. The operator identifies the uphill course; the catalogue picture also shows the southern return loop, which is excluded from this timed draft. Separate endpoint nodes agree with timing gates. This independent timed section measures 1,303.5 m while the catalogue scalar 2,019 m describes a longer extent; no return-road detour or coordinate scaling is used to match that number.

The aggregate catalogue picture identifies the outside road course only, with its full northern and southern extensions. The operator distinguishes this 2.4-mile outside course from the separate superspeedway and inside road course. Those other facilities are excluded. This diagram contains one independently mapped cycle, so it remains a regular route rather than a network with duplicate paths.

Full configuration keeps the triangular eastern return and continuous western bends, excluding the rounded extension and short internal loop. Its branches match the catalogue configuration picture. The circuit operator information identifies a 2.346 km circuit, consistent with the independent 2,338.4 m course; the catalogue scalar 2,491 m uses a different extent. The historical branch choice remains a draft.

Full rallycross perimeter retains the long upper branch and western sweeping return. The independently published circuit description states 1,135 m, consistent with this 1,136.0 m source route. The catalogue scalar 2,249 m differs substantially; its pictured circuit identifies the same venue perimeter. The source is not repeated or stretched to match that number. Normal and alternative-lap classification still needs review.

Rallycross main course uses the full northern straight and broad eastern return, excluding the shorter northern alternative. The event regulations identify a 1,088 m main lap and 1,070 m alternative lap; the independently mapped longer branch measures 1,079.2 m. The catalogue scalar 1,409 m differs. Course branches agree with the configuration picture; all coordinates remain exact source nodes.

Full rallycross perimeter uses the longer mapped northern branch and southern loop identified in the catalogue picture. Event regulations describe laps of 986 m and 978 m, consistent with the independently mapped 974.4 m draft rather than the catalogue scalar 1,440 m. Normal and joker branch classification remains provisional; no detour or repeated lap is added to reach the catalogue distance.

Full main rallycross circuit follows the northern long bend and southern projecting hairpin, excluding the upper alternative branch. The event operator identifies a 1,210 m course; the independent 1,202.5 m source loop agrees with that main-lap convention. The catalogue scalar 1,397 m differs and is not used to alter source coordinates. The pictured venue perimeter and timing position agree.

Full road circuit retains the northern perimeter, western inner hairpin and southern return, excluding the rectangular southern detour. These branches match the historical catalogue configuration picture. The operator records a 2,087 m configuration from 2005; this coarser independent mapped draft measures 1,993.3 m against the catalogue 2,102 m. That distance difference is retained for historical alignment review, not corrected by stretching coordinates.

The catalogue configuration retains the northwestern perimeter, the northern S bend, southeastern hairpin and the inner southern return. The actual connecting service way is present in the independently acquired venue snapshot. The route is measured at 2677.4 m versus the catalogue distance of 2686 m; the longer southwestern extension and short-cut branches are excluded.

The independently named Handling Circuit is a complete source cycle matching the single catalogue perimeter, without facility access roads or hill-route branches. Its measured distance is 1384.8 m versus the catalogue distance of 1389 m.

The independently named High Speed Bowl is the single full circular source cycle. Facility access and adjacent test roads are excluded. Source distance 3215.6 m versus the catalogue distance of 3223 m.

The identified airfield perimeter follows the western rectangular taxiway, northern eastbound return, broad northeastern turn and southeast-to-southwest perimeter. Interior runway shortcuts are excluded. Exact mapped runway/taxiway and road nodes measure 4772.6 m against the catalogue distance of 4795 m.

The longer northern perimeter and southern rectangular return match the catalogue configuration. The interior cutoff is not used. The independent airfield-centreline draft measures 770.1 m against the catalogue distance of 799 m and is visibly coarser at the bends.

The two complete dry-handling lobes and unbroken connecting curves match the catalogue configuration. Optional small chicanes in both lobes and the longer eastern variant are excluded. Independent source distance is 2178.1 m versus the catalogue distance of 2182 m.

The full double hairpin configuration retains the outer northern curve, inner parallel return and southern spiral. The sharper northern alternative, shortened southern return and cross-facility shortcuts are excluded. Exact independent service-road nodes measure 1886.9 m against the catalogue distance of 1865 m.

The full airfield circuit follows the long northern runway leg and southern perimeter with the central projecting return. Independently mapped runway and taxiway centrelines form an exact source cycle of 6691.8 m. The local council describes the proving-ground circuit as 6.5 km, while the supplied historical catalogue declares 7069 m. This draft retains the independently mapped course, documents that discrepancy and excludes the intermediate runway shortcut; historical alignment remains provisional.

The independently named Wet handling track forms one complete source cycle retaining the northern lobe, westward series of bends and southern return. The operator specifies 1517.5 m for the main circuit, close to the catalogue distance of 1519 m. The mapped OSM trace measures 1562.2 m and has a coarser southern return; the 2020 independent snapshot shows the same main alignment. This is a provisional draft, with the source distance preserved and historical bend detail still requiring review.

The independently mapped full course uses the complete north loop, inner return, long south straight and southeast outer hairpin; training cutoffs are excluded. Operator configuration photographs corroborate these major branch choices. Source bend detail remains provisional.

The independently mapped north course uses the complete northern loop and serpentine return; southern training roads are excluded. Operator configuration photographs corroborate these major branch choices. Source bend detail remains provisional.

Historical 2020 source preserves the original small northwest loop, central plateau, inner southeastern hairpin, outer southeast hairpin and uninterrupted southern straight. The enlarged current configuration is excluded. No source nodes are adjusted to match the supplied scalar distance.

The former street course follows the Estadi straight, Rosaleda and Santa Madrona bends, Guardia Urbana, Rius i Taulet and the former Marques de Comillas corridor. Current source roads provide a draft of the historical course, with modern junction alignment explicitly provisional; the internal Montanyans shortcut is excluded. Independent historical mapping corroborates the street sequence.

Road course retains Gerards Bend, the Esses, Shaws Hairpin and Devils Elbow, without Edwinas, Stapletons, Charlies or Bus Stop chicanes. This corrects the previous unreviewed relation association. The operator identifies a 1.35-mile configuration; the independent source line measures 2032.7 m and remains a draft with historical alignment provisional.

Plain oval retains Gerards Bend and the north oval shortcut, without Edwinas, Stapletons, Charlies or Bus Stop chicanes. This corrects the earlier distance-based hypothesis that followed added chicanes. The operator identifies a 1-mile oval; the independent source line measures 1551.7 m. The distance discrepancy is documented and no coordinates are altered.

Figure-of-eight course follows the independently named Chicago, Hammerhead, Follow-through, Bentley, Bacharach, Gambon, Crooner and Wilson sections. The two loops meet at an actual shared source node; no edge is duplicated and no crossing or connecting coordinate is invented. This preserves the crossing that a simple-cycle search omitted. Source length 2808.1 m remains unadjusted.

Pre-extension course follows the full northern bend, central return and southern hairpin using the pinned January 2018 raceways. Motorsport UK documents the later extension from 852 to 1140 m. The independently mapped historic route measures 850.4 m; current extension branches are excluded. Historical alignment and direction remain draft.

Earlier asphalt configuration follows the straight northern side, inner northeastern loop and full southern and southwestern bends. Northern zigzag alternatives and the eastern inner-loop shortcut are excluded. Independent source length 1063.8 m is preserved against the documented 1075 m configuration; this does not claim the later enlarged circuit.

Full northern hairpin and southeastern return use the southwestern chicane rather than the direct southern bypass or central shortcut. The independent source measures 839.2 m and retains its coarse corner geometry; no scaling to the supplied distance is applied. Configuration and direction remain draft.

International outer circuit follows the long northern bend, northeastern extension, inner central hairpin and full southern loop. The named operator course is 4085 m and the pinned independent route is 4085.9 m. Pit lanes, small western junction detours and shortened northern branches are excluded. Historical alignment and direction remain draft.

Full Italian Canyon course follows all fifteen numbered turns in the operator course map, including both western bends, the central inner loop, southern hairpin and long southeastern return. The Italian Canyon 2.7-mile configuration excludes the shorter mapped connector. The independent source length 4285.8 m is preserved, with the catalogue/operator distance discrepancy documented and no coordinate adjustment.

Full Grand Prix configuration uses the eastern chicane, northern bulb and complete western and southern loops. Alternative east-side shortcut and extra lower junction detours are excluded. Source length 5695.2 m remains unadjusted; configuration and direction remain draft.

Classic route follows Big Bend, Lefthander, Righthander, Paul Newman Straight, the original Climbing Turn, West Bend, Diving Turn and Sam Posey Straight. Optional South and West chicane branches are excluded, as shown by the operator classic-course map. The independently mapped length 2371.7 m is retained despite the supplied scalar-distance discrepancy.

The lake circuit follows the complete independently named Avenida Circuito del Lago, including its southern bends and the bridge section. Argentina tourism identifies this public-road circuit and access avenue; government documentation describes the 6.270 km historical course. The actual pinned road loop is 6172.4 m and remains unadjusted. Race-day barriers, chicane alignment and travel direction remain provisional; unrelated residential and service-road detours are excluded.

Dry Handling course follows the full long northern straight, eastern hairpin, two interior returns and southern chicane in the documented eleven-turn 3400 m operator circuit. The independent source tags its test-course segments as service roads; their connected full route is 3387.9 m. Wet-handling, skid-pad, noise-testing, access-road and triangular detour branches are excluded. All joins retain real source nodes, and direction remains draft.

The independently mapped West circuit follows its complete northern return, central inner loop, eastern West-course hairpin and southern chicane. The operator separate-circuit plan identifies these West branches and a nominal two-mile course; the actual source route is 3234.3 m. The East circuit, long alternative straight, pit and paddock roads are excluded. The catalogue distance of 3385 m is retained without changing source coordinates; alignment date and direction remain provisional.

The complete handling course follows all three arms and the central return bend shown in the published ADAC Schluesselfeld course plan.
